content_of_post_to_comment:
I’m 26 and I’ve had a pattern for most of my life that I’m finally trying to seriously address.

The frustrating part is that I usually know what I should be doing. I have goals, I can make plans, and I can understand logically what actions would move me forward. But when it comes time to actually sit down and consistently do difficult cognitive work, especially studying or professional work, I often feel this mental resistance/anxiety and start avoiding it.

I escape into things like my phone, social media, YouTube, overthinking, researching things I don’t really need to research, or even “productive” activities that aren’t actually the thing I should be doing.

This has affected me since school. I could often understand things well and people generally considered me smart, but I rarely studied as consistently as I could have.

The same pattern followed me into my professional life as a software engineer: sometimes doing things at the last minute, not learning as much as I should, or doing something just well enough instead of calmly working through it and producing high-quality work.

The strange thing is that I don’t seem to have the same problem with everything. I’ve trained/lifted and played sports consistently for years. I can diet, train hard and tolerate physical discomfort without needing someone to force me. It’s primarily studying, career-related work and other cognitively demanding things where this avoidance pattern becomes much stronger.

I’ve also noticed that anxiety makes it significantly worse. When something makes me feel pressure about my future, my instinct is often to seek distraction/reassurance rather than work directly on the thing causing the anxiety.

There are things from my childhood/past that I suspect could have contributed to this, including difficult experiences growing up, but I don’t want to diagnose myself or automatically blame everything on that.

I’m now actively trying to change the behavior. Some things I’m experimenting with are:
no recreational social media/YouTube during the first few hours of the day
putting my phone physically away while working
breaking work into concrete blocks instead of saying “I’ll work all day”
noticing when I’m escaping because of anxiety and returning to the task anyway
journaling to identify what triggers avoidance
deliberately practicing doing difficult work even when I don’t feel ready or motivated.

But I’m especially interested in hearing from people who recognize this pattern from their own life and genuinely became much better at dealing with it.

What actually made the difference?
Was it mostly behavioral changes and routines? Therapy? If therapy helped, what kind? Did you work with a psychologist, psychiatrist, therapist, coach, etc.? Did you discover something underlying the behavior that you hadn’t recognized before?

And most importantly: what did your day-to-day process of changing this actually look like?

I’m not looking for a diagnosis. I’m rather trying to hear experiences from people who spent years feeling like their own mind was getting in the way of what they were capable of doing, and eventually found something that substantially improved it.

What worked for you?
comment: I had a similar split where physical discipline felt natural but focused work felt impossible. What changed for me was treating avoidance as a habit loop, not a character flaw: notice the discomfort, reduce the first step until it’s almost boring, then start before my brain negotiates. I also found that tracking “did I show up?” mattered more than tracking output. The anxiety piece is worth exploring too.
